Q: How to export Wordpress posts database tables with polylang? A:

From what I'm understanding after spending a couple of hours searching for a similar answer myself, the Polylang plugin maps the languages by appending the language code "es" (for spanish) or "ar" (arabic) to the URL of the page and creates a new page.

To cross reference posts to language codes. If you look in the wp_term_taxonomy table and query

SELECT *
FROM `wp_term_taxonomy`
WHERE `taxonomy` LIKE "%translation%";

You will get a similar response to the below in the description column:

a:2:{s:2:"es";i:7149;s:2:"en";i:6534;}

Here we have language code "es" (for spanish) in post ID 7149, mapped to post ID 6534 for language code "en" (english). It's serialized PHP. You will need to unserialize the description column to get the post IDs:

array (
  'es' => 7149,
  'en' => 6534,
)

To upload your posts with the new translation, you would need to export all the records in wp_term_taxonomy which contain the "ar" AND "en" language codes in their description column.

After that, you need to pull the post IDs from the descriptions results query above. You can do this by generating a query using PHP which unserializes the description column data, and pulls both language codes' posts' IDs from the result.

You will need these table records to export your original and translated pages correctly:

1. The wp_terms_taxonomy records referencing all posts using your desired language codes in the description column. From this table you need the term_taxonomy_idand the description columns to retrieve records in the following two tables.

2. The wp_posts records referenced by the wp_terms_taxonomy records. (Query for these using the unserialized version of the description column in the wp_terms_taxonomy record as explained above).

3. With the post IDs you extracted in step 1, Use the same process to export the post ID (object_id column) and term_taxonomy_id (the foreign key to the description column's record) from the wp_term_relationships table. This wp_term_relationships table has the post_id and the taxonomy_term relationship which is used to retrieve the wp_terms_taxonomy record when the post is loaded. In other words, it relates post ids to taxonomy terms. You will get a record for each language code that share the same term_taxonomy_id. The object_id and term_taxonomy_id columns hold the post_id and the term_id that were extracted for the original and translated pages in step 1.

While Wrathyimp answer is partially correct, it fails to point out how exactly post_ids are cross referenced to language codes.

Q: Error running gluonfx:compile produces: $JAVA_HOME and $GRAALVM_HOME are undefined A:

The problem is:

The user xxx executes mybashrc to define the 2 environment variables

While,

root executes sudo mvn gluonfx:compile which has no access to environment variables defined by xxx

removing sudo executes mvn glunfx:compile as xxx

Q: Copy/Paste - From Mac to Virtual box A:

Below worked for me:

First check whether Guest Additions is the problem

Inside the Ubuntu VM, run:

lsmod | grep vbox
systemctl status vboxservice

If that shows nothing useful, Guest Additions is probably missing or broken.

Then install the packages Ubuntu usually needs before Guest Additions:

sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y build-essential dkms linux-headers-$(uname -r)

In the VM menu, click:

Devices → Insert Guest Additions CD Image

Then inside Ubuntu:

cd /media/$USER/VBox_GAs_*
sudo sh ./VBoxLinuxAdditions.run
sudo reboot

Guest Additions provides the shared clipboard integration VirtualBox depends on.

Then try text copy again

After reboot:

  • In the VM window, set Devices → Shared Clipboard → Bidirectional

  • Copy some plain text inside Ubuntu

  • Try pasting into a simple Mac app like TextEdit

If that still fails, check your VirtualBox version. If it is older than 7.1, and Ubuntu is using Wayland, upgrade VirtualBox and Guest Additions together because Wayland clipboard support was added in 7.1.

Q: File stuck in a staging area A:

What you probably want to do is reset the collection of staged files, then either

  • remove the file (file should not exist!)
  • ignore it (file is expected, but locally-managed)

A minor caution and feature (though it's not the case for you here) of the humble git reset without other qualifiers is that it will clear any added, but uncommitted changes, such as from git add --patch or later work you want to keep separate after some git add .
to separate them, you can reset by-path such as git reset -- dbstatus as I use below, though most users likely just say git reset and re-add when undoing some accidental additions

% git status  # show the staged files
On branch main
Your branch is up to date with 'origin/main'.

Changes to be committed:
  (use "git restore --staged <file>..." to unstage)
    new file:   dbhandler/test
% git reset -- dbhandler  # path is not required, unstaging all changes

% git status                                                                                                                                   20:06:48
On branch main
Your branch is up to date with 'origin/main'.

Untracked files:
  (use "git add <file>..." to include in what will be committed)
    dbhandler/test

nothing added to commit but untracked files present (use "git add" to track)

Then you can add the file to your .gitignore (takes immediate effect, but you should also commit your .gitignore) .. or delete the file

# contents of .gitignore
# ignore dbhandler/\357\277\275\357\277\275z
dbhandler/*

If you're just having trouble literally deleting the file, often a wildcard or "tab completion" will help you out, though I haven't used CMD or PowerShell in an extremely long time .. you can also just call explorer from wherever you are to get a Windows Explorer program window to delete the file with a UI

del "dbhandler/*z"
